q: Which garden type is characterized by symmetry, geometric shapes, and a clear central axis, using clipped hedges (topiary) to demonstrate human control over nature, exemplified by the Versailles Gardens?
n: Formal Gardens are characterized by symmetry, geometric shapes, and a clear central axis. They use clipped hedges (topiary) and precise paths to demonstrate human control over nature. Example: Versailles Gardens, France — displaying power and control through monumental landscape design.

q: Which functional purpose of softscape refers to adding color, form, texture, and fragrance?
n: Aesthetic Beauty adds color, form, texture, and fragrance.

q: Which tree shape has a 'narrow trunk widening into canopy' (e.g., Crape Myrtle), giving moderate shade good for small plantings?
n: The Vase-shaped tree has a narrow trunk widening into the canopy (e.g., Crape Myrtle), giving moderate shade good for small gardens and plantings.

q: What is the primary purpose of Retaining Walls?
o: To enhance sensory experience and promote tranquility
To hold back soil, especially on sloped landscapes, and to create level terraces for planting or entertaining
To define property boundaries and ensure privacy
To provide filtered shade and a vertical design anchor
n: Retaining walls hold back soil, especially on sloped landscapes, and create level terraces for planting or entertaining. They also add vertical dimension and visual interest, and can double as informal seating or raised garden beds.

q: What natural benefit do falling leaves provide, according to the source?
o: They create natural mulch, returning nutrients to the soil
They prevent all future plant growth
They eliminate the need for any soil at all
They permanently damage the landscape's hardscape
n: Falling leaves create natural mulch, returning nutrients to the soil.

q: Under 'Psychological and Emotional Impact,' where are landscaped areas said to be especially important for creating healing environments?
n: Landscaping creates healing environments especially in hospitals and schools, where landscaped areas provide restorative spaces.

q: Which garden type highlights water as the central design and ecological element, exemplified by Monet's garden at Giverny?
n: Water Gardens highlight water as the central design and ecological element, using ponds, aquatic plants, and fish (koi). Example: Giverny — Monet's Water Garden, inspired by his famous Water Lilies series, blending water and floral beauty.

q: What is UNITY in landscape design?
o: Ensuring the size of elements relates appropriately to each other
Achieving harmony by using consistent elements and themes throughout the landscape
Distributing visual weight evenly across a space
Drawing attention to a specific area using a distinctive feature
n: Unity is achieving harmony by using consistent elements and themes throughout the landscape.

q: What is SIMPLICITY in landscape design?
o: Creating movement and flow through repetition
Avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional
Ensuring elements relate appropriately in size
n: Simplicity is avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional.

s: Using Trees as Shade Elements — Tropical Climates
q: For tropical climates, what type of trees should be chosen to manage year-round heat and UV exposure?
n: Tropical climates: opt for dense evergreen trees to manage year-round heat and UV exposure.

q: What is the purpose of Edging and Borders in landscape design?
o: To hold back soil on sloped landscapes
To separate different landscape zones (e.g., garden beds from grass) and maintain neatness
To enhance sensory experience and promote tranquility
To provide filtered shade and a vertical design anchor
n: Edging and Borders separate different landscape zones (e.g., garden beds from grass) and maintain neatness.

q: Which materials are cited as typical hardscape materials?
o: Stone, concrete, wood, metal, bricks, tiles, and gravel
n: Hardscape materials include stone, concrete, wood, metal, bricks, tiles, and gravel.

q: Which garden type is designed to look natural but is highly planned, featuring winding paths, irregular clumps of trees, and hidden vistas to mimic a romanticized countryside?
n: Informal Gardens are designed to look natural but are highly planned. They feature winding paths, irregular clumps of trees, and hidden vistas to mimic a romanticized countryside, encouraging exploration and a sense of discovery.

q: How is Softscape defined?
o: Only the irrigation and drainage systems of a landscape
The lighting and sound systems used in outdoor design
All the living components of a landscape — the plants, soil, turf, and other organic materials
The non-living, solid, man-made elements of a landscape
n: Softscape refers to all the living components of a landscape — the plants, soil, turf, and other organic materials. These elements breathe life into a space and are typically dynamic, changing with the seasons, growing over time, and requiring active maintenance.

q: Which of the following is listed as a challenge of softscape?
o: It may be affected by climate, pests, or diseases, and needs seasonal planning and replacement
It never requires watering, pruning, or fertilizing
It requires no consistent care once installed
It cannot be affected by weather
n: Challenges of softscape include that it requires consistent care (watering, pruning, fertilizing), may be affected by climate, pests, or diseases, and needs seasonal planning and replacement.

s: Effects of Landscaping — Softens Hard Edges
q: Under 'Aesthetic Enhancement,' how does landscaping soften hard edges?
o: By removing all trees near a structure
By using organic elements to contrast and balance sharp building lines and materials like concrete or glass
n: Landscaping softens hard edges: organic elements contrast and balance sharp building lines and materials like concrete or glass.

q: What characterizes Deciduous Trees?
o: They remain evergreen year-round with needle-like leaves
They are chosen primarily for their flowers rather than shade
They have a single unbranched stem and a crown of fronds
They have a seasonal cycle, shedding all their leaves for part of the year
n: Deciduous Trees are characterized by their seasonal cycle, shedding all their leaves for part of the year.

q: Regarding leaf type and arrangement, what do broad leaves do compared to small or needle-like leaves?
o: Broad leaves block more sunlight, while small or needle-like leaves offer dappled or filtered light
Broad leaves offer only dappled light, while needle-like leaves block all sunlight
n: Broad leaves block more sunlight. Small or needle-like leaves offer dappled or filtered light.

q: Which of the following is listed among softscape's 'living materials'?
o: Trees, shrubs, flowers, grass, vines, groundcovers, and mosses
n: Living materials in softscape include trees, shrubs, flowers, grass, vines, groundcovers, and mosses.

q: Which tree shape is 'tall and narrow' (e.g., Italian Cypress, Palms), providing limited shade but useful for vertical framing, and is best used for borders and lining walkways?
n: The Columnar shape is tall and narrow (e.g., Italian Cypress, Palms), providing limited shade but useful for vertical framing; best used for borders and lining walkways.

q: Regarding seasonal behavior and sun shading, how do deciduous trees differ from evergreens?
o: Deciduous trees allow passive heating during colder months, while evergreens are consistent blockers
Deciduous trees block all sunlight year-round, while evergreens allow full sun in winter
Evergreens shed their needles in winter to allow passive heating
n: Seasonal Behavior: Deciduous trees allow passive heating during colder months; evergreens are consistent blockers.

q: Which tree shape is 'triangular or cone-shaped' (e.g., Pine, Spruce), giving shade at lower levels but with less broad canopy, and is best used for windbreaks and backdrops?
n: The Pyramidal/Conical shape is triangular or cone-shaped (e.g., Pine, Spruce), giving shade at lower levels but with a less broad canopy; best used for windbreaks and backdrops.

q: Which of the following describes softscape's environmental role?
o: It only provides a visual focal point with no ecological function
It prevents any wildlife from entering a landscape
It has no impact on stormwater or air quality
It absorbs water, purifies air, provides shade, attracts wildlife, and helps cool the environment
n: Softscape's environmental role includes purifying air, absorbing water, providing shade, attracting wildlife (birds, bees, butterflies), and helping cool the environment.

q: Regarding height and branch spread, what shading role do taller trees versus wider trees play?
o: Taller trees offer overhead shade, while wide trees provide lateral coverage
Both taller and wider trees serve identical shading roles
Height and spread have no bearing on shade coverage
Taller trees provide no shade, while wide trees offer only overhead shade
n: Taller trees offer overhead shade; wide trees provide lateral coverage.

q: How do softscapes evolve with time, according to the source's discussion of seasonality and change?
o: Softscapes bloom, shed leaves, and grow fuller or thinner over time
They only change if artificially watered
They lose all function once planted
n: Softscapes evolve with time — blooming, shedding leaves, growing fuller, or thinning out.

q: Which tree shape has 'downward drooping branches' (e.g., Weeping Willow), giving diffused shade and adding dramatic ambiance, best used near water features or meditative spaces?
n: The Weeping tree shape has downward drooping branches (e.g., Weeping Willow), giving diffused shade and adding dramatic ambiance; best used near water features or meditative spaces.

q: How does landscaping contribute to noise buffering, according to the source?
o: Plants and earth berms reduce noise pollution from streets or neighboring properties
Hardscape elements alone absorb all noise
Landscaping has no effect on noise levels
Only water features can reduce noise
n: Noise Buffering: plants and earth berms reduce noise pollution from streets or neighboring properties.

q: Regarding canopy density and sun shading, what does thicker foliage generally provide?
o: Better shade, as seen in trees like Narra, Acacia, and Mango, which excel in tropical climates
n: Canopy Density: thicker foliage means better shade. Narra, Acacia, and Mango are excellent examples in tropical climates.

q: What is the purpose of Structural and Decorative Elements such as pergolas, gazebos, benches, statues, and planters?
o: To purify air and manage stormwater runoff
To enhance style, provide support, or emphasize focal points in the landscape
To guide vehicles into driveways and parking areas
To hold back soil on sloped landscapes
n: Structural and Decorative Elements enhance style, provide support, or emphasize focal points in the landscape.

q: What characterizes Palm Trees, botanically?
o: They are monocots, often featuring a single unbranched stem and a crown of fronds
They are dicots with two embryonic leaves
n: Palm Trees are monocots (flowering plants whose seeds contain only one embryonic leaf, or cotyledon), often featuring a single unbranched stem and a crown of fronds. They are the hallmark of tropical and subtropical site design.

q: What is the purpose of Pathways and Walkways as a hardscape element?
o: To hold back soil on sloped landscapes
To enhance sensory experience and promote tranquility
To define property boundaries and ensure privacy
To guide movement, create flow, and define circulation routes throughout a landscape
n: Pathways and walkways guide movement, create flow, and define circulation routes throughout a landscape.

q: Which of the following is listed as a Key Characteristic of a garden?
o: It is always open to the public for free
It is artistic and botanical in nature, carefully arranged with themes such as color, plant species, or symmetry
It must always follow a formal, symmetrical layout
n: Key Characteristics of a garden include being artistic and botanical in nature, carefully arranged with themes (color, plant species, symmetry), and being more personal, intimate, and contemplative; gardens sometimes serve scientific or educational purposes.

q: What is SCALE in landscape design?
o: Natural or artificial lighting to highlight features and ensure safety
Water features, rustling plants, or birds enhancing ambiance
The relative size of landscape components to human scale and other elements
The layout and open/closed feeling of an area, and how areas are connected
n: Scale is the relative size of landscape components to human scale and other elements.

q: How is Hardscape defined?
o: Only the plumbing and irrigation systems beneath a landscape
The non-living, solid, man-made elements of the landscape that give structure, stability, and function
The living components of a landscape, such as plants and turf
The scientific classification of soil types
n: Hardscape involves the non-living, solid, and man-made elements of the landscape. These give structure, stability, and function to outdoor areas, forming the framework where softscape elements are arranged.

q: Which edging material is described as 'minimalist and long-lasting'?
n: Metal Edging is minimalist and long-lasting.

q: Under 'Integration and Sustainability in Design,' landscaping is described as integral to which green building certifications?
n: Sustainable Architecture: Landscaping is integral to green building certifications like LEED and BERDE.

q: Which garden type showcases lush, diverse vegetation through dense planting and a naturalistic layout, exemplified by the Baguio Botanical Garden?
n: Tropical Gardens showcase lush, diverse vegetation through dense planting, a naturalistic layout, and exotic species. Example: Baguio Botanical Garden — highlighting native Cordillera plants and traditional huts.

q: Under 'Functional Extension of Space,' what does landscaping accomplish by defining zones like patios, courtyards, and play areas?
o: Creating 'Outdoor Rooms' that extend living or working spaces outdoors
n: Landscaping can define zones like patios, courtyards, and play areas — extending living or working spaces outdoors as 'Outdoor Rooms.'

q: For passive solar design, where should broad-leaf deciduous trees be placed to block the most intense afternoon sun?
o: North and East sides of a building
South and West sides of a building
n: Broad-leaf deciduous trees should be placed on the South and West sides of a building to block the most intense afternoon sun.

q: Which pathway material is described as 'affordable and ideal for rustic or informal gardens'?
n: Gravel Trails are affordable and ideal for rustic or informal gardens.

q: Which functional purpose of hardscape means hardscapes often serve as focal points or design anchors?
n: Visual Anchor: hardscapes often serve as focal points or design anchors.

q: Which functional purpose of softscape is illustrated by different planting styles like tropical versus zen gardens evoking different emotions?
n: Mood & Atmosphere: different planting styles (e.g., tropical vs. zen garden) evoke different emotions and experiences.

q: What is SOUND in landscape design?
o: Using differences in color, texture, and shape to add interest
Water features, rustling plants, or birds that can enhance ambiance
The layout and open/closed feeling of an area
Distributing visual weight evenly across a space
n: Sound refers to water features, rustling plants, or birds, which can enhance ambiance.

s: Palm Trees — Effectiveness in Sun Shading
q: Unlike deciduous trees, what kind of shade do palm trees provide, and how should they primarily be used?
o: Dense, complete shade; as the primary passive cooling strategy for large facades
Dappled or minimal shade; primarily for aesthetic framing rather than passive cooling of large facades
Only shade during the dry season
No shade whatsoever; purely structural support
n: Unlike deciduous trees, palms provide 'dappled' or minimal shade. They should be used for aesthetic framing rather than as a primary strategy for passive cooling of large facades; they are often more effective when planted in naturalistic clusters rather than as single, isolated stalks.

q: What is the purpose of Fences and Screens as a hardscape element?
o: To highlight water as a sensory centerpiece
To guide vehicles into parking areas
To define property boundaries, ensure privacy, and block unwanted views or wind
To hold back soil on sloped landscapes
n: Fences and screens define property boundaries, ensure privacy, and block unwanted views or wind; they can also reduce noise pollution when lined with dense vegetation or sound-absorbing panels.

q: How does landscaping support Low-impact Development, according to the source?
o: By requiring high water use and heavy maintenance
By replacing all softscape with hardscape
Native and drought-resistant plants reduce water use and maintenance
By using only imported, non-native plant species
n: Landscaping supports Low-impact Development: native and drought-resistant plants reduce water use and maintenance.

q: In landscape design, which type of balance is described as 'formal'?
n: Symmetrical Balance is formal, distributing visual weight evenly on both sides of an axis.

s: Using Trees as Shade Elements — South-Facing Areas
q: For south-facing areas, which type of trees should be used for seasonal light control, providing shade in summer and sun in winter?
n: South-facing areas: use deciduous trees for seasonal control (shade in summer, sun in winter).

q: Because of their year-round density, what is the primary role of coniferous/evergreen trees?
o: Blooming for two weeks before appearing skeletal
Serving as the primary tool for creating windbreaks, reducing wind speed and lowering winter heating costs
n: Because they remain dense throughout the year, coniferous/evergreen trees are the primary tool for creating windbreaks. They can reduce wind speed significantly, lowering heating costs in winter, and their year-round density makes them ideal for screening unsightly views or dampening noise.

q: What challenge do ornamental trees present after their flowering period ends?
o: They immediately die and must be replaced
They may look 'skeletal' or sparse for the rest of the year
They become hazardous to walk beneath
n: An ornamental tree that looks stunning for two weeks of flowering might look 'skeletal' or sparse for the rest of the year. Some also shed fine, needle-like leaves that can clog drainage systems or pool filters more easily than larger leaves.

q: Which tree shape shows 'unstructured or wild growth' (e.g., Wild Guava), with shade that varies by size and may be uneven but rustic, best used in forested or naturalistic settings?
n: The Irregular/Natural shape shows unstructured or wild growth (e.g., Wild Guava); shade varies by size and may be uneven but rustic, best used in forested settings and naturalistic gardens.

q: Which type of park is described as the 'lungs of the city,' essential for physical and mental health, exemplified by Central Park in NYC?
n: Urban Parks are multifunctional green spaces within a high-density city, functioning as the 'lungs of the city' and essential for physical and mental health. Example: Central Park, NYC — a model of landscape architecture combining lakes, meadows, trails, and performance spaces within a bustling city.

q: What is RHYTHM in landscape design?
o: The layout and open/closed feeling of an area
The relative size of landscape components to human scale
Creating movement and flow by repeating elements like plants, colors, or paths
Avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional
n: Rhythm is creating movement and flow by repeating elements like plants, colors, or paths.

q: Why are palm trees considered ideal for tight urban spaces or planting near foundations and sidewalks?
o: They shed all their leaves in winter
They require no sunlight at all
Most palms have relatively small, non-invasive root balls and narrow trunks
They have massive, invasive root systems
n: Most palms have relatively small, non-invasive root balls and narrow trunks, making them ideal for tight urban spaces or planting near foundations and sidewalks.

q: In landscape architecture, what do the principles in landscape design serve as?
o: A checklist required for construction permits
A method for pricing hardscape materials
Guidelines to create aesthetically pleasing, functional, and sustainable outdoor spaces
A list of native Philippine plant species
n: The principles in landscape design serve as guidelines to create aesthetically pleasing, functional, and sustainable outdoor spaces.

q: According to the source, roughly how far apart should large trees be spaced, depending on canopy spread?
n: Large trees should be spaced 15–30 feet apart, depending on canopy spread.

q: Under 'Aesthetic Enhancement,' how does landscaping create visual harmony?
o: By complementing the architectural style, whether modern, tropical, minimalist, or classical
By ignoring the building's architectural style entirely
By using only a single plant species throughout
n: Landscaping creates visual harmony by complementing the architectural style (modern, tropical, minimalist, classical).

q: What is SPACE in landscape design?
o: The layout and open/closed feeling of the area, and also how areas are connected
Natural or artificial lighting to highlight features
The relative size of landscape components to human scale
n: Space is the layout and open/closed feeling of the area; also how areas are connected.

q: Which pathway material is described as 'popular in gardens or residential yards; natural and textured'?
n: Stone Pavers are popular in gardens or residential yards, and are natural and textured.

q: What is the purpose of Water Features in landscape design?
o: To enhance sensory experience, promote tranquility, and serve as a visual centerpiece
To separate different landscape zones and maintain neatness
To guide movement through paths, stairs, and ramps
To hold back soil on sloped landscapes
n: Water features enhance sensory experience, promote tranquility, and serve as a visual centerpiece. They balance the solidity of the landscape with movement and reflection.

s: Effects of Landscaping — Improves Air Quality
q: Under 'Environmental Benefits,' how does landscaping improve air quality?
o: Landscaping has no effect on air quality
Plants release pollutants into the air
Plants absorb pollutants and release oxygen
n: Landscaping improves air quality: plants absorb pollutants and release oxygen.

q: Besides expense and risk of dominating a design, what other challenge does hardscape present, according to the source?
o: It needs proper drainage and surface planning to avoid water pooling or flooding
It requires seasonal replacement like plants
It cannot be combined with softscape elements
n: Hardscape needs proper drainage and surface planning to avoid water pooling or flooding.

q: Which structural element 'provides filtered shade and a vertical design anchor'?
n: Pergolas and Gazebos provide filtered shade and a vertical design anchor.

q: Which functional purpose of hardscape is described as guiding movement through paths, stairs, and ramps?
n: Accessibility & Flow guides movement through paths, stairs, and ramps.

q: Which garden type has the purpose of plant conservation, education, and display, exemplified by the Singapore Botanic Gardens?
n: Botanical Gardens are purposed for plant conservation, education, and display, using design elements like scientific plant labeling, arboretums, and thematic zones. Example: Singapore Botanic Gardens, a World Heritage site with an orchid garden and rainforest trail.

q: What are Ornamental/Flowering Trees chosen primarily for?
o: Their root systems' ability to prevent erosion
Their aesthetic qualities — flowers, foliage color, bark texture, or unique canopy shapes
Their ability to serve as windbreaks
n: Ornamental trees are chosen primarily for their aesthetic qualities — flowers, foliage color, bark texture, or unique canopy shapes. They are used primarily for decorative value and sometimes partial shading.

q: What distinguishes a deck from a patio, according to the source?
o: Decks are typically elevated and made of wood or composite materials, while patios are ground-level and made from stone, brick, or concrete
Decks are ground-level and made of stone; patios are elevated and made of wood
Decks and patios are identical in every respect
Patios are always more expensive than decks
n: Decks are typically elevated and made of wood or composite materials, while patios are ground-level and made from stone, brick, or concrete.

s: Using Trees as Shade Elements — Driveways or Walkways
q: For driveways or walkways, which tree shapes are recommended to avoid blocking paths?
n: Driveways or walkways: use columnar or vase-shaped trees to avoid blocking paths.

q: Which decorative patio type 'imitates stone or brick at a lower cost with high design flexibility'?
n: Stamped Concrete Patios imitate stone or brick at a lower cost with high design flexibility.

q: According to the source, hardscape is not just the 'frame' for landscaping — what else does it define?
o: The zoning laws that apply to a property
How a space works, how people move through it, and how comfortable, inviting, and expressive it can be
Only the cost of a landscaping project
The botanical classification of the plants used
n: Hardscape is not just the 'frame' for landscaping — it defines how a space works, how people move through it, and how comfortable, inviting, and expressive it can be.

q: How have many palm species evolved to survive high-wind events like typhoons?
o: Through flexible trunks and aerodynamic fronds
n: Many palm species have evolved to survive high-wind events (like typhoons) due to their flexible trunks and aerodynamic fronds.

q: Which tree shape is 'dome-like on top, slightly taller than wide' (e.g., Mango, Rain Tree), giving good overhead shade with less horizontal coverage, and is best used for driveways and patios?
n: The Oval/Umbrella shape is dome-like on top, slightly taller than wide (e.g., Mango, Rain Tree), giving good overhead shade with less horizontal coverage; best used for driveways and patios.

q: What is EMPHASIS (Focal Point) in landscape design?
o: Drawing attention to specific areas using distinctive features like a sculpture, fountain, or tree
Achieving harmony by using consistent elements throughout
Using differences in color, texture, and shape to add interest
Distributing visual weight evenly across a space
n: Emphasis (Focal Point) is drawing attention to specific areas using distinctive features like a sculpture, fountain, or tree.

q: How is a Garden defined in the source material?
o: An intentionally cultivated area primarily focused on plants, aesthetics, and beauty, which can be private or public and often carries symbolic, cultural, or meditative meaning
A large, planned area of land open to the public for recreation
A protected tract of land managed only by the government
A paved commercial space for vehicles
n: A garden is an intentionally cultivated area primarily focused on plants, aesthetics, and beauty. Gardens can be private or public, and their design often carries symbolic, cultural, or meditative meaning.

q: Which of the following is given as an example of a Deciduous Tree?
o: Maple, Oak, Narra, Mahogany, or Acacia
n: Examples of Deciduous Trees include Maple, Oak, Narra, Mahogany, and Acacia.

q: Which garden type focuses on spiritual contemplation, using dry elements like raked sand (representing water) and carefully placed rocks (representing mountains), exemplified by the Ryoan-ji Garden in Kyoto?
n: Japanese Zen Gardens are focused on spiritual contemplation, using dry elements like raked sand (representing water) and carefully placed rocks (representing mountains). Their purpose is meditation, reflection, and Zen Buddhism. Example: Ryoan-ji Garden, Kyoto — a world-renowned dry landscape garden meant for contemplation.

q: Under 'Climate Control and Thermal Comfort,' how do trees and pergolas help minimize the need for air conditioning?
o: By blocking all natural light entirely
By providing shade, which reduces heat gain, lowers surrounding temperatures, and minimizes the need for air conditioning
By eliminating the need for any ventilation
n: Trees and pergolas provide shade, reducing heat gain, lowering surrounding temperatures, and minimizing the need for air conditioning.

q: Which functional purpose of hardscape is illustrated by retaining walls preventing soil erosion and pergolas providing shade?
n: Structural Support: retaining walls prevent soil erosion; pergolas provide shade.

q: Which pathway material is described as 'classic, patterned paths often used in colonial or traditional settings'?
n: Brick Walkways are classic, patterned paths often used in colonial or traditional settings.

q: Among the key elements to consider in landscape design, what does TEXTURE refer to, as illustrated by rough bark versus soft grass?
o: The surface quality of materials or plants
The shape of plants and structures
n: Texture is the surface quality of materials or plants (e.g., rough bark vs. soft grass).

q: Among the key elements to consider in landscape design, what does FORM refer to?
o: Sets mood and visual interest, impacting seasonal appeal
The shape of plants and structures, e.g., columnar trees, rounded shrubs
Surface quality of materials or plants, e.g., rough bark vs. soft grass
n: Form is the shape of plants and structures (e.g., columnar trees, rounded shrubs).

q: What is a key maintenance challenge of fruit-bearing trees like Mango?
o: They cannot survive in tropical climates
High-fructose fruit drop can stain concrete, tiles, and parked cars, and attract ants, flies, and rodents if not harvested
They require no watering at all
n: Fruit drop can stain concrete, tiles, and parked cars. High-fructose fruit (like Mango) attracts ants, flies, and rodents if not harvested. Many fruit trees also have aggressive, thirsty root systems that can crack nearby foundations or sidewalks, so they are best kept in 'soft' areas away from high-traffic paths and parking.

q: Besides plants, what organic components does softscape include?
n: Organic components of softscape include not just the plants, but also soil types, compost, and mulch.

q: Which hardscape material for driveways and parking areas is 'textured and slip-resistant'?
n: Exposed Aggregate Concrete is textured and slip-resistant.

q: By roughly what percentage can a well-landscaped property boost real estate value, according to the source?
n: A well-landscaped property can boost value by up to 15–20%.

q: Which hardscape material for driveways 'allows water to seep through, supporting sustainability'?
n: Permeable Pavers allow water to seep through, supporting sustainability.

q: Which type of fence uses trellises or lattices that support climbing plants like bougainvillea or jasmine?
n: Living Screens (with hard frames) are trellises or lattices that support climbing plants like bougainvillea or jasmine.

q: What is BALANCE in landscape design?
o: Creating movement and flow by repeating elements like plants, colors, or paths
Using differences in color, texture, and shape to add interest
Avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional
Distributing visual weight evenly, which can be symmetrical or asymmetrical
n: Balance is distributing visual weight evenly. This can be Symmetrical Balance (formal) or Asymmetrical Balance (informal but still visually stable).

q: Which water feature 'may include aquatic plants, koi fish, or lily pads'?
n: Ponds may include aquatic plants, koi fish, or lily pads.

q: How is a Park defined in the source material?
o: A large, planned area of land, often managed by a government or private organization, open to the public for recreation, rest, and social engagement
A private garden focused on plants and meditation
A dry landscape garden used exclusively for religious ritual
A single vacant lot converted into a parking area
n: A park is a large, planned area of land, often managed by the government or a private organization, that is open to the public for recreation, rest, and social engagement. Parks are designed for multipurpose use and integrate both natural and artificial elements.

q: Which of the following is listed as a Key Characteristic of a park?
o: It is exclusive to paying members only
It is inclusive and community-oriented, and is multi-zoned for various activities such as sports, concerts, and walking
It serves only a single, fixed function
It cannot host cultural or community events
n: Key Characteristics of a park include being inclusive and community-oriented, multi-zoned for various activities (sports, concerts, walking), often part of urban planning to provide green relief in cities, and promoting social equity by offering free public space.

q: Which retaining wall material is 'organic and blends into hilly landscapes'?
n: Natural Stone is organic and blends into hilly landscapes.

s: Using Trees as Shade Elements — Courtyards and Patios
q: For courtyards and patios, which broad canopy or umbrella trees are recommended, such as Rain Trees or Acacias?
n: Courtyards and patios: use broad canopy or umbrella trees like Rain Trees or Acacias.

q: Among the key elements to consider in landscape design, what does LINE refer to?
o: Sets mood and visual interest, impacting seasonal appeal
Defining edges, guiding movement, and shaping the layout, e.g., pathways or plant borders
The surface quality of materials or plants
The shape of plants and structures, such as columnar trees or rounded shrubs
n: Line defines edges, guides movement, and shapes the layout (e.g., pathways, plant borders).

q: Which functional purpose of hardscape allows for outdoor dining, relaxation, cooking, or entertaining?
n: Usability allows for outdoor dining, relaxation, cooking, or entertaining.

q: Which type of park consists of large tracts of land protected by the government for their natural, semi-natural, or developed state, exemplified by Palawan Underground River Park?
n: National Parks are large tracts of land protected by the government for their natural, semi-natural, or developed state, with a function of protecting natural heritage and biodiversity. Example: Palawan Underground River Park, PH — a UNESCO site known for biodiversity and sustainable tourism.

q: What characterizes Coniferous/Evergreen Trees?
o: They typically have needle-like or scale-like leaves, produce cones, and mostly retain their foliage year-round
They shed all their leaves seasonally
They are chosen mainly for fruit production
They have a single unbranched stem and a crown of fronds
n: Coniferous/Evergreen Trees typically have needle-like or scale-like leaves and produce cones. Most are evergreen, meaning they retain their foliage year-round.

q: Which of the following is listed as a challenge of hardscape?
o: It is generally cheaper to install than softscape
It can become too dominant or sterile if not balanced with softscape
It requires no drainage or surface planning
It cannot serve as a focal point
n: Challenges of hardscape include that it is more expensive to install and modify, and it can become too dominant or sterile if not balanced with softscape.

q: Which fruit-bearing tree species are noted for providing 'some of the thickest, most effective thermal buffers against tropical heat'?
n: Species like Mango or Star Apple (Caimito) provide some of the thickest, most effective thermal buffers against tropical heat.

q: What is LIGHT in landscape design?
o: Natural or artificial lighting to highlight features and ensure safety
The relative size of landscape components to human scale
Creating movement and flow by repeating elements
Water features, rustling plants, or birds that can enhance ambiance
n: Light is natural or artificial lighting used to highlight features and ensure safety.

q: What is the sun-shading effectiveness of coniferous/evergreen trees best suited for?
o: Framing vistas without any shading value
Consistent sunshade throughout the year; best for areas needing constant shading or privacy
n: Coniferous/evergreen trees provide consistent sunshade throughout the year, and are best used for areas needing constant shading or privacy.

q: Which of the following is given as an example of an Ornamental/Flowering Tree?
o: Cherry Blossom, Jacaranda, Palawan Cherry, or Fire Tree
n: Examples of ornamental/flowering trees include Cherry Blossom, Jacaranda, Palawan Cherry, and Fire Tree.

q: In landscape design, which type of balance is 'informal but still visually stable'?
n: Asymmetrical Balance is informal but still visually stable, distributing visual weight unevenly yet in equilibrium.

q: Which tree shape is described as having a 'wide and symmetrical canopy,' with examples like Narra and Acacia, giving wide, even shade over large areas?
n: The Round/Spreading shape has a wide and symmetrical canopy (e.g., Narra, Acacia), giving wide, even shade over large areas; best used for yards, plazas, and parks.

q: Which type of park consists of small-scale spaces often created on a single vacant lot or a small corner of a city block, functioning as 'micro-retreats' in dense cities?
n: Pocket Parks are small-scale spaces often created on a single vacant lot or a small corner of a city block, functioning as micro-retreats in dense cities. Design considerations include efficient use of limited space, low-maintenance plants, and seating.

q: Which of the following is listed as a built element of hardscape?
o: Walkways, patios, retaining walls, pergolas, decks, driveways, fences, fire pits, and water features
n: Built elements of hardscape include walkways, patios, retaining walls, pergolas, decks, driveways, fences, fire pits, and water features.

q: What is the dual purpose of Fruit-bearing Trees, which are considered staples of 'Edible Landscapes'?
n: Fruit-bearing trees provide fruit and shade, turning a site from a passive space into a productive one — the staples of 'Edible Landscapes.'

q: What is CONTRAST AND VARIETY in landscape design?
o: Creating movement and flow by repeating elements
Avoiding clutter by keeping the design clean and intentional
Using differences in color, texture, and shape to add interest
Ensuring the size of elements relates appropriately to each other
n: Contrast and Variety is using differences in color, texture, and shape to add interest.

q: Which functional purpose of softscape supports biodiversity, manages stormwater runoff, and improves air quality?
n: Ecological Benefits: supports biodiversity, manages stormwater runoff, and improves air quality.

q: Which type of park is focused on entertainment and commercial recreation, with design considerations like ride safety and immersive storytelling, exemplified by Magic Kingdom at Walt Disney World Resort?
n: Theme Parks function for entertainment and commercial recreation, with design considerations including ride safety, fantasy architecture, and immersive storytelling. Example: Magic Kingdom at Walt Disney World Resort, Florida.

q: How does landscaping manage stormwater, according to the source?
o: By paving over all permeable surfaces
Only through underground concrete drainage pipes
Rain gardens, green roofs, and permeable surfaces reduce runoff and prevent flooding
n: Landscaping manages stormwater: rain gardens, green roofs, and permeable surfaces reduce runoff and prevent flooding.

q: In temperate or subtropical climates, how do deciduous trees behave across the seasons?
o: They retain foliage year-round and block all sunlight in winter
They provide dense canopy shade in summer, and their bare branches allow sunlight to penetrate and warm the building in winter
They provide no shade at any time of year
They only bloom and never produce broad leaves
n: In temperate or subtropical climates, deciduous trees provide dense canopy shade in summer, reducing solar heat gain on facades; in winter their bare branches allow sunlight to penetrate and naturally warm the building.

q: What is PROPORTION in landscape design?
o: Creating movement and flow through repeated elements
Ensuring that the size of elements relates appropriately to each other and to the overall space
Drawing attention to specific areas using distinctive features
n: Proportion is ensuring that the size of elements relates appropriately to each other and to the overall space.

q: Which retaining wall material is described as metal cages filled with rocks, giving an 'industrial and rugged look'?
n: Gabion walls are metal cages filled with rocks, giving an industrial and rugged look.

q: Among the key elements to consider in landscape design, what does COLOR refer to?
o: Sets mood and visual interest, and impacts seasonal appeal
The surface quality of materials or plants
The shape of plants and structures
n: Color sets mood and visual interest, and impacts seasonal appeal.

s: Effects of Landscaping — Urban Heat Island Effect
q: How does landscaping help reduce the Urban Heat Island Effect?
o: By adding more asphalt and concrete surfaces
By increasing the number of paved parking lots
Green surfaces cool the surroundings through evapotranspiration and shade
By eliminating all green spaces in a city
n: Landscaping reduces the Urban Heat Island Effect: green surfaces cool the surroundings through evapotranspiration and shade.
